Explore /home/cis/windows/realstate — a Next.js 16 App Router / React 19 real estate site. We're planning to add: (a) a full-screen 3D voice-agent onboarding gate that appears before the site, (b) a scroll-driven 3D building-construction sequence, and (c) a scrollable 3D apartment interior walkthrough. I need to understand the page/routing structure and where these would slot in.

Search breadth: very thorough.

Read and report in detail on:
1. `app/layout.tsx` (already partly known — focus on provider nesting order and where a new gate/overlay would mount) and `app/page.tsx` (the home page section-by-section structure).
2. `app/projects/[slug]/page.tsx` — this is the biggest page (379 lines). Report its full section structure, what components it renders in what order, its `generateMetadata`, `generateStaticParams`, and every dynamically-imported block. Quote the JSX skeleton.
3. `components/projects/deferred-*.tsx` (deferred-brochure, deferred-floor-plans) and `components/finance/deferred-emi-calculator.tsx`, `components/forms/deferred-enquiry-form.tsx` — the dynamic-import/deferral pattern used. Quote one fully.
4. `components/projects/floor-plan-viewer.tsx` (324 lines) — how the SVG floor plan viewer works, its zoom/pan/keyboard handling. This is relevant because a 3D interior view may replace or augment it.
5. `components/projects/unit-matrix.tsx`, `progress-timeline.tsx`, `cost-sheet.tsx`, `rera-block.tsx` — brief summary of each.
6. `lib/floor-plans.ts` — the schematic floor plan data model. Quote the type definitions and one example layout.
7. `lib/placeholders/projects.ts` — the project data shape as actually populated. Quote ONE full project entry so I can see all fields with real values.
8. Report whether there is any localStorage/sessionStorage/cookie usage anywhere (grep) — relevant for remembering the user's name after the onboarding gate.
9. Report any existing client-side state management, context providers, or user-personalization anywhere in the app.

Quote code verbatim where it matters. I need enough detail to plan major additions without re-reading these files.

===§7===
## 7. WebGL / Three.js Guardrails

Treat the viewport as a cinematic film set, not a toy.

- **Materials:** PBR `MeshStandardMaterial` with real roughness/metalness/normal maps (e.g.
  metalness 0.8 / roughness 0.2). Never flat unlit meshes.
- **Lighting:** architectural-studio setup — soft ambient occlusion, subtle directional light with
  shadow mapping (`<ambientLight intensity={0.5} />` + `<directionalLight castShadow />`).
- **Post-processing:** subtle SSR, controlled bloom, chromatic aberration, film grain, vignette.
- **Camera:** no jarring cuts or free-roam (motion sickness). Dampened lerp / GSAP drone-like reveals.
- **Budgets:** hero scene <100k triangles, <30 draw calls; DPR capped at 1.5.
- **Assets:** Draco/meshopt-compressed GLTF; KTX2 or WebP textures (GPU-direct, no CPU decode).
- **Memory:** never allocate inside `useFrame`/rAF (`new THREE.Vector3()` → GC stutter). Instantiate
  vectors/matrices once and recycle. Pause rAF when offscreen (IntersectionObserver) and on tab blur.
- **Threading:** offload the Three.js pipeline to a Web Worker via **OffscreenCanvas** so shader
  compilation/geometry parsing never blocks the main thread (keeps INP <200ms).
- **Loading:** wrap `<Canvas>` in `dynamic(() => import(...), { ssr:false })` — never block LCP.
  Reserve container dimensions with CSS `aspect-ratio` to prevent CLS.
- **Fallbacks:** mobile / low-power / reduced-motion get a high-res static WebP or `<video poster>`
  instead of the 3D scene.
- **Progressive enhancement is mandatory:** real H1, body copy and links live in server-rendered HTML
  behind/around the canvas. Bots read HTML, not WebGL pixels.

---

## 8. Page-by-Page Spec

**HOME** — (1) cinematic hero: subtle R3F scene or poster + muted-autoplay video, editorial headline
with SplitText reveal, real H1 in server HTML, static fallback on mobile. (2) Trust bar: years/legacy,

## 7. WebGL / Three.js Guardrails

Treat the viewport as a cinematic film set, not a toy.

- **Materials:** PBR `MeshStandardMaterial` with real roughness/metalness/normal maps (e.g.
  metalness 0.8 / roughness 0.2). Never flat unlit meshes.
- **Lighting:** architectural-studio setup — soft ambient occlusion, subtle directional light with
  shadow mapping (`<ambientLight intensity={0.5} />` + `<directionalLight castShadow />`).
- **Post-processing:** subtle SSR, controlled bloom, chromatic aberration, film grain, vignette.
- **Camera:** no jarring cuts or free-roam (motion sickness). Dampened lerp / GSAP drone-like reveals.
- **Budgets:** hero scene <100k triangles, <30 draw calls; DPR capped at 1.5.
- **Assets:** Draco/meshopt-compressed GLTF; KTX2 or WebP textures (GPU-direct, no CPU decode).
- **Memory:** never allocate inside `useFrame`/rAF (`new THREE.Vector3()` → GC stutter). Instantiate
  vectors/matrices once and recycle. Pause rAF when offscreen (IntersectionObserver) and on tab blur.
- **Threading:** offload the Three.js pipeline to a Web Worker via **OffscreenCanvas** so shader
  compilation/geometry parsing never blocks the main thread (keeps INP <200ms).
- **Loading:** wrap `<Canvas>` in `dynamic(() => import(...), { ssr:false })` — never block LCP.
  Reserve container dimensions with CSS `aspect-ratio` to prevent CLS.
- **Fallbacks:** mobile / low-power / reduced-motion get a high-res static WebP or `<video poster>`
  instead of the 3D scene.
- **Progressive enhancement is mandatory:** real H1, body copy and links live in server-rendered HTML
  behind/around the canvas. Bots read HTML, not WebGL pixels.
